etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English loser, losere, equivalent to lose +‎ -er. In the sense of contemptible or worthless individual, perhaps an alteration of losel, which see.

definitions.definition: A person who loses; one who fails to win or thrive.
(informal, US) A person who is frequently unsuccessful in life.

quote.citation: 2012, Frank Shamrock, Charles Fleming, “Fatherhood”, in Uncaged: My Life as a Champion MMA Fighter, Chicago Review Press, →ISBN, page 203:
quote.text: Mike didn't work but insisted that Jewell have a job.  He would stay home and do whatever — smoke pot, screw around. He was a total loser, and she picked up the slack. That's around the time that Mom met her soon-to-be-next husband. He immediately moved in. He was a loser, too, with the same work ethic Mike had.

definitions.definition: One who or that which loses something, such as extra weight, car keys, etc.

quote.citation: 1999, Larry Medsker, Lakhmi C. Jain, Recurrent Neural Networks: Design and Applications, →ISBN, page 192:
quote.text: Another way to speed search (in general) is to order or bias the hypothesis space based on some heuristic. Suppose you are a habitual car key loser and that you keep track of where your keys turn up after each search.

quote.citation: 2004, Marianna S. Katona, Tales from the Berlin Wall: Recollections of Frequent Crossings, →ISBN:
quote.text: But a West German reporting a lost passport in East Berlin during the years of the Wall was treated to a criminal investigation, with the passport loser as the potential criminal.

quote.citation: 2009, Jane Bryant Quinn, Making the Most of Your Money Now:
quote.text: You're counting on this insurance company to pay you a check many years in the future. But for some companies, disability coverage has been a money loser.

quote.citation: 2010, Cutting Myself in Half: 150 Pounds Lost, One Byte at a Time, →ISBN, page 109:
quote.text: You have to think of yourself as an already amazing person who's hiding behind extra weight—a superhero in a disguise. If you follow the program,  […]  change the message from “I'm a big loser” to “I'm a big weight loser.”

definitions.definition: A losing proposition, one that is likely to lose or already has lost (such as a losing bet or, analogously, a predictably fruitless task or errand).

quote.citation: 1988, Alice Taylor, To School Through the Fields: An Irish Country Childhood, Brandon Ltd, →ISBN, page 58:
quote.text: A new Guard came to town and decided to flex his muscles with George. We could have told him that he was on a loser but bright young men, then as now, know it all.

quote.citation: 2001, Peter Svoboda, Beating the Casinos at Their Own Game‎[1], Square One Publishers, →ISBN, page 57:
quote.text: Hardway bets are losers if they are rolled in any other combination—called "soft" or "easy" numbers. For instance, a Hardway bet on a 4 is a loser if the dice show as 3 and 1. Betting on a Hard 8 is a loser if the dice are rolled as a 5 and 3, or a 6 and 2. Naturally, if the 7 is rolled before the Hardway number shows, the bet is also a loser.

quote.citation: 2021 December 17, Eric Ralph, “SpaceX to replicate Starbase, build multiple Starship launch pads in Florida”, in Teslarati‎[2], retrieved 2022-08-07:
quote.text: In terms of betting on outcomes, Mars is a clear loser.

definitions.definition: (slang) A person convicted of a crime, especially more than once.
